html:
José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia was the dictator of Paraguay from 1814 until his death in 1840. He was called El Supremo, the Supreme One.

A doctor of theology, he led the young republic after independence and was named perpetual dictator in 1816. To protect Paraguay from Buenos Aires and Brazil, he closed its borders, allowing little trade or travel. He broke the power of the Spanish-born elite and the Church, took their lands for the state, and is said to have forbidden Europeans to marry each other.

His rule made Paraguay self-sufficient, with state farms and no foreign debt, but also silent and afraid. He trusted no one and left no successor. The novelist Augusto Roa Bastos made him the subject of his masterpiece, I, the Supreme. Later rulers such as Carlos Antonio López opened the country again.
sum: José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia was the dictator of Paraguay from 1814 until his death in 1840. He was called El Supremo, the Supreme One.
